body:
It's not really clear what's going on in the videos you shared, so I'd recommend turning on grid display so we can see what's happening. If it's the same as the issue you linked, then this looks like it's specific to odd-sized, offset or centered pixel textures, but it's most obvious with `CollisionShape2D` which is always centered. Keep in mind, any time you use centered, odd-sized textures in a small pixel game, you're going to have artifacts in game too since you're trying to render sub-pixels.

I don't believe this is the right fix, since this just removes the feature rather than correcting it. From some testing, it looks like this was working correctly (or at least consistently) in 4.3, but broke somewhere along the way. Also, there are two places where we use this setting, and this only changes one of them. 

4.3 vs 4.5:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16213d86-531f-4209-87ba-d9e20dd1112c

From some testing, it looks like this was working correctly (or at least consistently) in 4.3, but broke somewhere along the way. Also, there are two places where we use this setting, and this only changes one of them.

This doesn't remove the feature, it turns it off inside the editor. Snapping will continue to work as expected while running in-game.

This behavior is in line with other game-exclusive viewport scaling features of the engine - they never happen inside the editor. Doesn't that make this fix the intended behavior?

> This behavior is in line with other game-exclusive viewport scaling features of the engine - they never happen inside the editor. Doesn't that make this fix the intended behavior?

The intended behavior (and what's asked of in the linked issue) is what's displayed in the above video before a bug was introduced. If it's preferred that the feature is disabled in the editor even when working correctly, that's cool, but should have a proposal. There's definitely precedent for certain features being hidden in the editor. Though, the PR in its current state only half removes it from the editor, and even if it were fully removed, it would only hide the fact that there's still an underlying bug that was introduced between 4.3 and now that broke the snapping. It'd be better to fix the bug, then decide if we want the feature in the editor.
